- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior 30d mean.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% above recent 18-day high), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending down, model frequently fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 18-day moving average or 30d median.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.53) and recent price action shows downward momentum; add 1–3% to forecast to account for hidden bearish sentiment.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is below 65% of 30d mean, model often misses the bottom; apply a “floor” correction to prevent underestimation in bearish regimes.
- When sentiment is high but price is falling, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 1–4% to avoid “overbought” overreaction.
